title: About
text:
History of BRaVe
The first version of BRaVe, a fully static desktop-based version, was launched in 2014 and has seen continued use since then. More recently a mobile version, internally referred to as BRaVe 2, was piloted in Somalia and a number of countries. In August 2025, development began on BRaVe 3, a comprehensive rearchitecturing and rebuild of the system, replacing both version 2 and 3, with a subsequent launch in 2026. The first open source release of BRaVE was in June 2026.

title: How-to Guides
text:
2 Setup






ImportantWho does what



Setup tasks happen in two places. Each section below is labelled accordingly.








Label
Where
Who




PORTAL
BRaVe Management Portal (web browser)
Administrator / Programme Officer


MOBILE
BRaVe mobile app (Android phone or tablet)
Enumerator


DESKTOP
BRaVe Card Printing App (Windows PC with card printer)
Card printing operator



These labels are used throughout this guide, not only in the Setup section.




2.1 Before you begin
You will need:

A BRaVe tenant for your mission, created by the BRaVe support team. Each mission runs in its own tenant so its data is isolated.
A portal account with the Program Admin role (IOM staff sign in with their IOM account; implementing partners use the Partner login).
The portal address for your environment:

Testing/UAT: https://testportal.brave.iom.int
Production: https://portal.brave.iom.int

For device setup: the Android phones or tablets you will use in the field, with the BRaVe app installed and provisioned (linked to your tenant). See How to install BRaVe in the Device Management section.







Note



Biometric capture is optional and configurable per activity. Devices only need a fingerprint scanner if your activities require biometrics.




2.2 Portal setup PORTAL

2.2.1 How to sign in to the Management Portal

Open the portal address in your browser.
Choose a login method: click IOM Staff Login (authenticates with your IOM Microsoft account) or Partner Login for implementing-partner accounts (Figure 1).
Complete the multi-factor authentication prompt if requested.







Figure 1: The portal login page. Staff and partners use separate logins.



After signing in you land on the Dashboard. The left-hand menu follows the operational workflow from top to bottom: Users, Registration, Deduplication, Targeting, Assistances, Data Exchange, Configuration and Monitoring (Figure 2).






Figure 2: The portal dashboard. Setup tasks live mainly under Configuration.





2.2.2 How to set up a registration programme
Every mission needs at least one registration programme. The programme records the purpose of the registration and carries the Risk Benefit Assessment (RBA), which must be approved before activities can start.

In the left menu, open the Programs page.
Click to add a new programme and complete the RBA form: the purpose of the registration activity, target population groups, who data will be shared with, and where it takes place.
Submit the programme. It goes through an approval process; its status is shown in the programme list (Figure 3).
Once the status is Approved, you can add activities to the programme.







Figure 3: The programme list. Each programme shows its RBA status and a Manage Activities action.









Tip



If your mission has already completed a risk assessment outside BRaVe, the support team can transpose your existing programme into the system.




2.2.3 How to configure activities
Activities are the working unit of BRaVe: registrations, record checks and distributions all happen within an activity. Think of activities as buckets — create as many or as few as you need.

From the programme list, click Manage Activities on an approved programme.
Click + Setup Activity (Figure 4).
Give the activity a title, description, and start and end dates.
Attach the configuration the activity needs:

one or more consent forms (multiple languages are supported, e.g. Portuguese);
the household-level and individual-level surveys to use;
preferences, such as whether biometrics are collected in this activity;
the enumerators allowed to work in it (the whitelist).

Save the activity. BRaVe assigns it a short activity code (e.g. 8GZ9) — enumerators use this code to download the activity onto their devices.







Figure 4: Activities within a programme. Each activity has a code, title and active dates.









Note



Consent forms and surveys are attached per activity, so different activities can collect different data — for example biometrics in one activity and none in another.




2.2.4 How to create distribution items, kits and distribution types
If you will use BRaVe for assistance delivery, configure what is distributed before the distribution starts. The hierarchy is: item types (e.g. tarpaulin, rope) are grouped into kit types (e.g. Emergency Shelter Kit), which are attached to a distribution type (e.g. Emergency Shelter Distribution).

In the left menu, open the distributions configuration page. It has three tabs: Distribution Types, Kit Types and Item Types (Figure 5).
On Item Types, create the individual items with their SKU, unit of measure (UoM) and quantity.
On Kit Types, create kits and add items to them.
On Distribution Types, click + Add Distribution Type and name the distribution.
Open Manage Items on the new distribution type and use + Add Kit to this distribution or + Add Item to this distribution to define what each beneficiary receives (Figure 6).







Figure 5: The distribution configuration page, with tabs for distribution types, kit types and item types.









Figure 6: An Emergency Shelter Kit attached to the Emergency Shelter Distribution. Use View Composition to check the items inside the kit.





2.2.5 Other first-time configuration






WarningScreenshots to be added



The following setup tasks are done in the portal (mostly under Configuration) but are not yet illustrated in this guide. They will be documented in their own how-to guides:

How to provision devices — link each phone or tablet to your tenant; each device gets a device code (e.g. OGAA04).
How to add enumerators — create the enumerator profiles (each gets a code such as EN05) that appear on provisioned devices; enumerator access has an expiry date and can be set inactive.
How to configure administrative areas — load the admin boundaries used in registration.
How to add lookups and data fields — reference lists and custom data points.
How to create surveys — build the household- and individual-level questionnaires attached to activities.
How to configure preferences — mission-wide defaults such as biometric capture.






2.3 Device setup {#device-setup} MOBILE
Once the portal setup is complete and devices are provisioned, each enumerator prepares their own device. This takes a few minutes and needs connectivity; after the activity is downloaded, registration can run fully offline.

2.3.1 How to log in as an enumerator

Open the BRaVe app on a provisioned device. The login screen shows the device code in the title bar, and the environment (e.g. UAT) it is linked to (Figure 7).
Tap Search Enumerator and type your enumerator code (e.g. EN05) or name, then select yourself from the list (Figure 8).
Tap Continue.
The first time you log in, set a secure 4-digit PIN. On later logins, enter your PIN (Figure 9).







Figure 7: The app login screen. Check the device code and environment badge before continuing.









Figure 8: Searching the enumerator list by code.









Figure 9: Each enumerator protects their account with a 4-digit PIN.



After logging in you see the dashboard. It is empty until you download an activity and start collecting data (Figure 10).






Figure 10: The mobile dashboard summarises the enumerator’s own progress per activity.





2.3.2 How to download a field activity onto the device

From the dashboard, open the Field Activity List.
Tap the download button (bottom right).
Enter the activity code given to you by the programme officer, then tap OK (Figure 11).
The activity appears in your list with its title, description and active dates (Figure 12).
Tap Refresh on the activity before going to the field so the device holds the latest configuration (surveys, consent forms, enumerator whitelist).







Figure 11: Enumerators pull activities onto the device with the short activity code.









Figure 12: Downloaded activities, each with Refresh (pull latest configuration) and Sync (push collected data).









NoteRefresh vs Sync



Refresh pulls the activity’s latest configuration to the device. Sync pushes collected registration data from the device to the portal — run it at the end of each day, or whenever you have connectivity.




2.3.3 How to verify an activity is ready for fieldwork
Before travelling to the field, open the activity and confirm it is configured correctly:

In the Field Activity List, tap the activity to open its details.
Check the Enumerator Whitelist contains everyone working in this activity (Figure 13).
Check the Consents section lists the right consent form(s), with the correct required/optional flag and language.
Check the Surveys section shows the expected household and individual surveys and their required/optional status (Figure 14).
Confirm the action buttons at the bottom match the work planned: Registrations, Biometric Record Check and/or Distributions.







Figure 13: Activity details: whitelist, preferences and consent forms.









Figure 14: Activity details: surveys and the available actions.



If anything is missing, correct the activity in the portal, then tap Refresh on the device.

title: How-to Guides
text:
3 Registration and data management
Registration is the point where people enter the BRaVe database. Enumerators collect data in the mobile app; administrators design the forms beforehand and manage the resulting records afterwards in the portal.






NoteRegistration hierarchy



BRaVe registers households, then adds individuals to them. A household record holds the household ID, size, type and location; each individual holds biographical data, an optional photo and optional biometrics. Surveys can be attached at either level.



3.1 Conducting a registration MOBILE
The steps below assume you are logged in as an enumerator and have downloaded the activity onto your device (see Device setup). The whole workflow runs offline — you only need connectivity to sync afterwards.

3.1.1 How to register a household

Open the activity from the Field Activity List and tap Registrations.
Tap Add Household. The New Registration form opens with the Household ID and Activity Code already filled in — the household ID is generated from the device code, so IDs never clash between devices (Figure 15).
Enter the Household Size and select the Household Type (e.g. IDP).
Tap Collect under Location Coordinates to capture GPS coordinates. The accuracy is shown next to the reading (Figure 16).
Optionally add Household Location free-text address detail.
Enter a Registration Token only if your operation issues pre-printed tokens; otherwise leave it blank.
Tap save.







Figure 15: The New Registration form. Household ID and activity code are pre-filled.









Figure 16: After saving, the household shows its captured coordinates and accuracy. Use the person icon to start adding members.









Tip



If GPS accuracy is poor, tap Clear and Collect again once you have a better sky view. The reading shown as ±100.0 m is the accuracy radius, not an error.




3.1.2 How to add individuals to a household
A household record is not complete until it has members. Repeat this procedure for every person in the household.

From the saved household, tap the add person button.
If the activity has a required consent form, it appears first. Read it to the respondent and record their answer — YES to proceed, NO to stop (Figure 17). Multiple consent forms can be configured, and they appear in sequence.
On the Add Individual screen, enter the first name, optional middle name and last name (Figure 18).
Enter the date of birth, or use the Years / Months / Days fields if the person only knows their approximate age.
Select the Relationship to the head of household and the Gender (Figure 19).
Tap the camera button to take a photo, if photos are collected in this activity (Figure 20).
Tap save.







Figure 17: Required consent forms are shown before any personal data is collected.









Figure 18: The Add Individual form. Age can be given as a date of birth or as years/months/days.









Figure 19: Relationship and gender are selected from configured lists.









WarningConsent first



Do not begin data collection before the consent response is recorded. If the respondent declines, stop the registration for that individual.




3.1.3 How to capture biometrics
Biometrics are optional and switched on per activity. When enabled, the Photo & Biometric section offers a fingerprint button alongside the camera.

Save the individual first. The biometric option becomes available on the saved record (Figure 20).
Connect the fingerprint scanner and tap the fingerprint button.
Place the finger on the scanner. The capture app extracts the minutiae and confirms Extraction succeeded (Figure 21).
Tap Add to keep the capture, or Retry if the quality is poor. Use Set position to record which finger was scanned.
Repeat for each finger your operation captures.
Return to the individual record. A warning reads “Biometric changes detected. Don’t forget to save your changes.” — tap save (Figure 22).







Figure 20: The Photo & Biometric section of an individual record.









Figure 21: A successful fingerprint capture. Retry if quality is poor before tapping Add.









Figure 22: Biometric changes must be saved explicitly on the individual record.









NoteHow many fingers?



Capturing more fingers improves deduplication but takes longer per person. Two thumbs is a common compromise and aids cross-agency deduplication; ten digits is the most robust. Decide this before fieldwork starts and apply it consistently.
If a fingerprint cannot be captured, record why using the Reason Biometric Was Not Captured field rather than leaving it blank.




3.1.4 How to complete surveys
Surveys attached to the activity appear as separate forms, marked Required or Optional.

Open the individual record and tap the survey button to complete the individual-level survey. Questions may be dropdowns, numeric inputs or multi-select lists (Figure 23).
Return to the household level and complete the household-level survey the same way (Figure 24).
Save each survey when finished.







Figure 23: An individual-level survey, e.g. accessibility and health questions.









Figure 24: A household-level survey, e.g. shocks experienced and coping strategies.









Note



Both survey levels are optional in BRaVe, and an activity can carry more than one of each — useful when you want a short core form for everyone plus a longer module for a sample of households.




3.1.5 How to sync registrations to the portal
Data stays on the device until you sync. Records are not visible in the portal, and cannot be deduplicated or targeted, until this step is done.

Go back to the Field Activity List.
Tap Sync on the activity (Figure 25).
Wait for the sync to finish before closing the app.







Figure 25: Sync pushes collected registrations from the device to the portal.









Important



Sync at the end of every collection day, or whenever you have connectivity. Unsynced data exists only on the device and is lost if the device is lost or damaged.





3.2 Printing beneficiary cards DESKTOP
Card printing runs in a separate BRaVe Card Printing App on a Windows machine connected to a card printer (e.g. Zebra ZC300). It downloads records from the portal, prints, and reports back which cards were produced.

3.2.1 How to print beneficiary cards

Open the BRaVe Card Printing App and confirm the Selected Printer shown at the top right (Figure 26).
Choose how to find records:

Household ID — print for a single household;
Activity — load everyone registered under an activity code;
Upload File — supply a text file listing the households to print.

Enter the value and click LOAD RECORDS. The list shows each person’s name, family size, household ID, activity, and whether a card has already been printed (Figure 27).
Tick the records to print. Records already marked Printed are blocked to prevent duplicate cards, unless an administrator authorises a reprint.
Select a Template. Missions can hold several card designs.
Click PREVIEW CARD to check the layout, then PRINT CARD and confirm.
When printing is finished, click SYNC TO SERVER so the portal records which cards were printed.







Figure 26: The BRaVe Card Printing App, showing printer selection, template and print actions.









Figure 27: Records loaded by activity code. The Printed and Locked columns prevent double printing.









WarningAlways sync after printing



Printed cards are flagged locally until you sync. If two machines print from the same list before syncing, the same person can receive two cards. Sync as soon as a print run finishes.








Note



Cards can be reprinted (for example, when a card is lost or damaged), but this is a controlled action. Some missions use tokens instead of cards — card printing is optional and configured per mission.





3.3 Managing registration data PORTAL






CautionDraft — not yet verified against the live portal



The four procedures below were not covered in the source demo recording. They describe the intended workflow and must be checked against the live portal, and screenshotted, before this section is published. Treat field names and button labels as provisional.



3.3.1 How to create a custom registration form
Registration forms in BRaVe are built as surveys and then attached to an activity, so the same form can be reused across activities.

In the portal, go to Configuration and open the surveys page.
Create a new survey and set its level: Household or Individual. This determines whether it is answered once per household or once per person.
Add questions, choosing a field type for each:

short text, long text and numeric fields;
single-select and multi-select lists (drawn from lookups);
date fields;
yes/no fields.

Set validation rules per question — required or optional, and minimum/maximum values or lengths where relevant.
Add conditional logic where a question should only appear based on an earlier answer (for example, only ask about pregnancy if gender is female).
Add translations for each question so enumerators can switch language in the field.
Save and publish the survey, then attach it to an activity (see How to configure activities).







Tip



Keep required questions to a minimum. Every required field slows down each registration, and at scale a single extra question adds hours of fieldwork.




3.3.2 How to edit a beneficiary record

In the portal, go to Registration and search for the record by household ID, name or activity.
Open the record and select Edit.
Update the biographical fields as needed. Household-level and individual-level data are edited separately.
To re-enrol biometrics — for example when the original capture was poor — flag the record for re-enrolment; the next time an enumerator opens it on a device, they can capture new fingerprints.
Save the record. All changes are written to the audit trail, which records what changed, who changed it and when.







Important



Records are personal data. Edit only what you can justify, and record the reason where the form allows it — the audit trail is reviewed during data protection audits.




3.3.3 How to merge duplicate records
Merging is the resolution step after deduplication has flagged two records as the same person. See the Deduplication section for how matches are found and adjudicated.

Open the flagged pair from the deduplication queue.
Compare the two records side by side. BRaVe highlights the fields that differ and shows supporting indicators (biometric match score, shared attributes).
Decide which record survives. Normally this is the earlier registration, so the original registration date is preserved.
For each conflicting field, choose which value takes precedence. Prefer the value that is more complete or more recently verified.
Confirm the merge. The surviving record keeps a link to the merged record, and the merge is written to the audit trail.







Warning



Merging is not easily reversible. Where the evidence is ambiguous — common when few people hold ID documents and names are spelled inconsistently — leave the pair unresolved and escalate rather than guessing.




3.3.4 How to bulk import beneficiary data
Bulk import brings in beneficiaries registered outside BRaVe, for example from an earlier Kobo exercise.

In the portal, go to Data Exchange and choose the import option.
Download the import template so your file has the expected columns.
Prepare your data as CSV or Excel, one row per individual, with a household identifier column linking members of the same household.
Upload the file and map each column in your file to the corresponding BRaVe field.
Run a dry run first. BRaVe validates the file without writing anything and reports errors by row and column.
Fix any validation errors in the source file and re-run the dry run until it is clean.
Run the import. Imported records enter the same deduplication workflow as records registered on a device.

title: How-to Guides
text:
4 Deduplication PORTAL
Deduplication finds people who have been registered more than once. BRaVe supports two approaches, which are complementary rather than alternatives:








Approach
Matches on
Available when




Biometric
Fingerprint minutiae, scored numerically
Biometrics were captured during registration


Field-based
Configurable rules over registration data (names, age, documents, phone)
Always — the only option for imported or non-biometric records



Both approaches produce candidate matches. A candidate match is a suggestion, not a decision. A human then adjudicates it — confirming the two records are the same person, or rejecting the match.






ImportantThere is no silver bullet



Deduplication quality depends on the data available. Field-based matching struggles where few people hold identity documents or phones, names are spelled inconsistently, and ages are approximate. Biometric matching is far more reliable but requires fingerprint capture. Expect a residue of ambiguous pairs in any operation, and plan adjudication time accordingly.



4.1 How to do biometric deduplication and adjudication
Biometric deduplication runs automatically. A background service processes fingerprints as soon as registrations are synced to the portal, so matches are usually waiting for you rather than something you trigger.

4.1.1 How to review the biometric match queue

In the left menu, open Deduplication and select the biometric matching page. The Deduplication / Biometric matching tab lists every candidate pair, with the total number of records at the top (Figure 28).
Narrow the list using the filters if needed:

Activity Code — restrict to one registration activity;
Date From / Date To — restrict by registration date;
Minimum Score — hide low-confidence pairs.

Click Apply. Use Clear to reset the filters.
Read each row as a pair: the source record on the left, the matched record on the right, and the Biometric Score between them. Each side shows registration date, activity code, age, gender and a link to the household.
Click View Match Details on a pair to adjudicate it.
Use Export to Excel if you need the queue offline, for example to divide adjudication work across a team.







Figure 28: The biometric match queue. Each pair carries a biometric score — here 105 and 482.





4.1.2 How to adjudicate a match
The Match Details screen presents everything needed to decide, and records the decision.

Compare the Source Record and Matched Record side by side (Figure 29). Check the photo, name, age, gender, household size, household ID and registration date. Click an image to compare photos directly.
Click View History under Match History to see whether either record has been adjudicated before.
Check the Match Location Map. It plots where each registration took place and gives the distance between them — 1.21 km in the example. A short distance supports a genuine duplicate; a very large distance is worth questioning.
Expand More information on either record for the full registration detail.
Work through the Deduplication indicators checklist and select every option that applies (Figure 30). The indicators are arranged as opposing pairs:

biometric match high (score ≥ 200) / biometric match low (score < 200);
no biometric, manual deduplication;
household names matching / completely different household names;
same gender / different gender;
matching age / age difference within 5 years / age gap between 5 and 10 years / age gap over 10 years;
matching family members / some matches in family members / completely different member names and ages.

Click Generate Suggestion. BRaVe proposes an action based on the indicators you selected.
Decide: Confirm Match if the records are the same person, or Reject Match if they are not.







Figure 29: Match Details: source and matched records side by side, with a map showing the distance between registration points.









Figure 30: The deduplication indicators checklist and the Confirm / Reject actions.









WarningThe suggestion is advisory



Generate Suggestion summarises the indicators you ticked — it does not make the decision for you, and it cannot see anything you have not recorded. The adjudicator remains responsible for the outcome.
Where evidence conflicts — a strong biometric score but completely different household composition, for example — do not force a decision. Leave the pair and escalate it.








Note



Confirmed matches feed the merge workflow, where you choose which record survives and which field values take precedence. See How to merge duplicate records in Registration and data management.




4.1.3 How to flag a record for review
Records can also be flagged outside the match queue, for example when an enumerator reports a problem.

Go to Monitoring and open the Raw Data page.
Filter by mission, programme, activity and date range, then click Apply. You can also search by household, head name, mission or activity.
Tick the records concerned and click Flag for review (Figure 31). Flagged records show in the Flagged column.
Use View Details to open a record, or Export CSV to take the list offline.







Figure 31: The Raw Data page, used to review registrations and flag records.






4.2 How to do field-based deduplication and adjudication






CautionSection incomplete — walkthrough required



The field-based deduplciation part will be added shortly.








TipWhy field-based matching still matters



Every record imported from another system arrives without fingerprints, and some operations choose not to collect biometrics at all. In both cases field-based matching is the only deduplication available — so the rules deserve careful design even where biometrics are the primary method.

text:
9 Device Management

9.1 How to load the Neurotechnology license MOBILE

Using a laptop, USB cable, Bluetooth, or file transfer method, copy the two Neurotechnology license files into the Licenses folder. Navigate to the device storage and create the following folder path if it does not already exist:
/Neurotechnology/Licenses
Log in to the BRaVe app using a Supervisor Enumerator account.
On the dashboard, tap the three dots in the top-right corner.









Figure 32: Tap the three dots on the dashboard.










Figure 33: Select Activation from the dashboard menu.






Select Activation.
Next to License Server, tap Activate.
A folder browser will open. Navigate to the device storage and select the folder:
/Neurotechnology/Licenses
If the licenses are valid, they will automatically be loaded.
Under Licensing, disable Use Trial Mode.
Restart the application.
Once activation is successful, the product will be activated and ready for use.



9.2 Guidelines before uninstalling BRaVe Mobile App MOBILE
If you need to completely uninstall the application (hard uninstall) or clear app data:

Open the app first and check the BRaVe version.









Figure 34: Check the BRaVe app version.










Figure 35: Tap the three dots on the dashboard.










Figure 36: Tap Activation.






Log in using a Supervisor Enumerator account.
On the dashboard, tap the three dots in the top-right corner.
Tap Activation on the drop-down menu.
Go to the Activation tab where you should see a list of active licenses.
Select the license and click Deactivate.









Figure 37: Deactivate the Neurotechnology license.










Figure 38: Uninstall the BRaVe app.






Exit and close the BRaVe app.
Uninstall the BRaVe app. Press and hold the BRaVe app icon and select Uninstall.







WarningImportant



Failure to deactivate the license before uninstalling may result in the license remaining locked to the previous installation or device state. This will corrupt the license and need Neurotechnology to fix it.




9.3 How to reactivate the BRaVe Mobile App license MOBILE

Install the new version of BRaVe on the mobile device.

Using a laptop, USB cable, Bluetooth, or file transfer method to copy the BRaVe app to the mobile device.
